summary.intent: Autonomously run the full post-execute-phase ship loop (verify, secure, validate, simplify, SDK E2E gate, CodeRabbit review, ship, resolve PR reviews, extract learnings) for GSD phase 69 (FUSE/WinFsp Rust integration and grant-root awareness), triaging findings without babysitting.
summary.outcome: PR #594 opened with all standard CI checks green (including cargo-windows after the user pushed the missing 69-14 Windows platform work) and all 9 review threads resolved, but the user-added Desktop E2E hard gate caught a real cross-client decryption bug — the Rust FUSE mount encoded NodeContent.file_iv as hex while the TS/web reference used base64 — which was root-caused by a delegated debugger and a fix was being committed at the end of the session.

repo: NodeContent.file_iv must be base64 (TS/web contract); the Rust FUSE mount was encoding it as hex, causing every cross-client (SDK) content decrypt to fail with GCM tag failure while the mount's own reads passed (self-consistent hex round-trip)

The node-codec KAT's sample file_iv value (000102030405060708090a0b) is coincidentally valid as both hex and base64, so it never caught the encoding mismatch — needs a KAT that discriminates the two encodings

cargo-windows CI failures (47 compile errors) were entirely from the unexecuted plan 69-14 (Windows platform layer, autonomous:false/D-06) calling stale pre-node/v3 function signatures in crates/fuse/src/platform/windows/*
This repo squash-merges PRs, so branch commit message format never reaches release-please post-merge; only the PR title and pr-release-preview.js's pre-merge parse matter
.github/scripts/pr-release-preview.js regex tolerates parens in commit descriptions and skips merge commits — it only rejects the non-conventional `feat NN-NN:` (space) subject format
gh pr edit fails on this repo due to Projects-classic GraphQL; must PATCH the PR body via `gh api -X PATCH repos/.../pulls/<N> -F body=@file`
markdownlint excludes .planning/ in CI but prettier still runs on it
After gh pr create (and after a passing Release Preview), github-actions[bot] pushes a chore(release) commit — must git fetch+rebase before the next push or it's rejected
CodeRabbit CLI times out summarizing full-phase diffs (125 files/24k lines); scoping via --dir to net-new directories (crates/sdk, crates/fuse, crates/core) works and surfaces real findings
CodeRabbit CLI free tier rate-limits after a few scoped reviews (~46 min wait) — fall back to the PR-level review for remaining scopes

Desktop E2E (desktop-e2e.yml) is workflow_dispatch-gated and does not run automatically on PR pushes, so a cross-platform/cross-client regression like the file_iv encoding bug can ship through all normal CI checks undetected

Prior debug doc d07-write-plane-pairing.md documents a related bug: FUSE node identity derived from client-local inode (uuid_from_ino) mismatched across clients/moves; fix c4d30e598 addressed identity but was never re-verified via desktop-e2e until this session

code.finding: is_unresolved predicate duplicated the enclosing cid.is_empty() check, making it always true and the pending_content/empty-file fallback unreachable — caused read-after-write to return EIO instead of serving buffered content
Derived Debug on InodeKind leaked key material because Zeroizing forwards its inner Debug impl; replaced with a manual redacting Debug impl

enforce_resolved gates on an 'attempted' generation value; for fetch_node_gated's own-resolve path this is deliberately the locally-trusted floor (not the fetched node's own generation), by design mirroring the TS dfsFindFolder rule — floor-vs-floor comparison is intentional, not a bypass, since forged records are still caught by the IPNS-signed (seq, CID) binding

Root cause of cross-client decrypt failures: publish_file_node emitted hex-encoded file_iv while fetch_and_decrypt_content_async and the TS SDK expect base64; fixed to base64 on both publish and decode paths
Journaled placeholder NodeContent.file_iv also needed to switch from hex to base64 to match the fixed content_ops.rs publish path

workflow: Run heavy test suites (cargo test --workspace) centrally from the orchestrator, never concurrently from parallel subagents — they starve RAM

When CodeRabbit/Greptile findings touch security/crypto-critical code, spawn parallel adversarial-verification agents per finding cluster (REAL/FALSE/DEFER) rather than blind-applying fixes; this caught at least one FALSE finding that would have damaged a desync-sensitive write path
For deep, multi-step debugging (stack bringup, reproduction, root-cause) delegate to a dedicated subagent with full accumulated context rather than doing it inline as orchestrator

Triage rule 'in-scope+low-risk → fix now; pre-existing/out-of-scope/risky → todo + note in PR' scales well for autonomous review triage across ~40+ findings from multiple sources (verifier, security auditor, CodeRabbit, Greptile)

Static code analysis alone can be inconclusive for cross-language crypto bugs — needed to trace an already-applied fix (c4d30e598) plus actual CI failure logs to conclude a second, distinct root cause existed

friction: Security auditor subagent stalled mid-stream ('API Error: Response stalled') after ~7.5 minutes with no output written, forcing the orchestrator to assemble the SECURITY.md report manually from raw threat-register data
git commit hung/timed out due to 1Password SSH signing, falsely reporting commit_failed when the commit had actually landed — required verifying via git log before retrying
zsh treats $status as a read-only variable, breaking a background poll script that used it as a custom var name
GitHub GraphQL mutations (reply/resolve review threads) failed silently on first attempts; required re-running with visible error output and retries to confirm success
gh api log retrieval for failed CI runs returned empty/delayed content, requiring multiple attempts to get the actual failure tail
CodeRabbit CLI could not review the full 125-file phase diff (timed out) and later got rate-limited on the apps/desktop scope, requiring workaround scoping and reliance on the later PR-level review
Desktop E2E gate (added mid-session at user's request) is slow (~30-45 min per matrix run) and had to be dispatched twice — once before 69-14 landed (Windows leg failed to compile) and once after
open_items: SC#3 shared-scope-exit rotation (ROT-07) is fail-closed but not live-wired to a production RotationDeps implementor — tracked as a deferred todo, not yet fixed
SDK floor-store non-atomic read-modify-write (mirrors the shipped TS twin's known behavior) captured as a deferred concurrency/atomicity todo
FUSE publish/concurrency hardening items (journal_helpers key-hygiene Zeroizing promotion, dead clone, CAS-retry consolidation, Windows-keying hardening) captured as a deferred todo
node-codec KAT should be hardened to pin file_iv encoding (hex vs base64) so a similar cross-language encoding regression can't slip through again — captured as a todo

The file_iv base64 fix (content_ops.rs, journal_helpers.rs, docs/METADATA_SCHEMAS.md) was committed by the debugger's findings but not yet pushed, and the Desktop E2E workflow had not yet been re-dispatched to confirm the fix at the point the transcript ends

Full headless local FUSE-T round-trip test was not run to validate the fix locally (per project convention, CI's warm stack is treated as authoritative for these reads) — authoritative confirmation still pending a CI desktop-e2e re-run
